text:
maria: FYI I'm hitting a confusing packaging/install issue with the Python SDK when people use Poetry editable installs. Reproducer: `poetry install` in the sampleapp, then `python -c 'import redwood_sdk; import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` -> ModuleNotFoundError for redwood_sdk.asyncio. The wheel/install produced by CI seems fine, but editable mode hides the subpackage.

sam: Is this the new PEP 660 editable mode (poetry delegates to pip)? We saw similar where `poetry install` results in an editable wheel that doesn't include package_data or properly map packages because of [tool.poetry.packages] omission. Can you paste pyproject.toml?

maria: Snippet:```toml
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
description = "Redwood Python SDK"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.8"
```
But we actually rely on having `redwood_sdk/asyncio` and `redwood_sdk/typing` subpackages. When I run `pip wheel .` locally I see the wheel has the subpackages, but `poetry install` editable result ends up with an egg-link-like layout where the package root is installed but some subpackages can't be imported (very inconsistent across dev machines).

josh: Two things to check: 1) Is there a top-level namespace package (PEP 420) or implicit namespace usage? That can confuse editable installs. 2) Poetry/core editable backend had a bug that omitted packages if `include` globs didn't match directories exactly.

maria: Not using explicit namespace packages. Structure is normal: `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/asyncio/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/typing/__init__.py`.

sam: Can you run `python -c 'import importlib, pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.walk_packages(redwood_sdk.__path__)))'` in both a normal pip install and the poetry editable env and compare? That usually shows what's actually on sys.path. Also try `pip show -f redwood-sdk` inside the venv to see installed files.

maria: Good call — in poetry env it shows only `redwood_sdk/__init__.py` and none of the subpackages. `pip show -f` lists very few files.

dev-bot: CI job #4821 failed building wheel on macos-latest-arm: "ERROR: Invalid wheel tag for platform" — linked log: https://ci.example/4821

josh: That CI error is a separate build matrix mismatch, but could be related to how we generate universal wheels vs platform-specific compiled artifacts. However the editable issue smells like packaging metadata. For a concrete fix, change pyproject to use the `packages` table with explicit include patterns:```toml
[tool.poetry.packages]
include = "redwood_sdk"
from = "src" # if using src layout
``` If you're not using src layout remove `from`. Also ensure you run `poetry self update` — older poetry versions had editable/P660 regressions.

katie: Another recurring gotcha: missing `py.typed` file in package root breaks typing consumers and some installers might prune files. Are you shipping `py.typed`?

maria: We do have `py.typed` in repo root but maybe not included in the packaging manifest. Our tests don't catch editable mode differences.

sam: Workarounds: - `pip install -e .` works reliably for editable mode (uses setuptools PEP 660 implementation differently). - For poetry, add a `tool.poetry.include` entry for `py.typed` and ensure `packages` covers subpackages. Example:```toml
include = ["redwood_sdk/**", "py.typed"]
```

maria: Confirmed `pip install -e .` works locally. `poetry install` still broken unless I add the explicit include. Will push a tiny PR updating pyproject.

josh: Also add a CI job to run `poetry install` + unit tests in an isolated env to avoid regressions. We should also document recommended dev workflows (pip editable vs poetry editable) in devex docs.

katie: I'll open a small PR with docs and a test matrix entry. Also suggest adding a packaging smoke test that does `python -c 'import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` after install.

maria: I'll open the pyproject change and include `py.typed`. Thanks — I'll link the PR here when ready.

josh: minor note: some users reported a different issue with macOS ARM wheel tags when wheel is built on remote runner with musl vs glibc mismatch — not related to the editable bug but worth tracking (CI failure linked above).

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/1287 (adds explicit packages include + py.typed + poetry docs). Can someone review?

sam: Reviewing now. Also add a changelog note under dev docs about editable quirks.

katie: Reviewing + will add the CI smoke test in a follow-up PR. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks everyone, closing the loop for now. If the fix doesn't work for some contributors I'll collect minimal repro steps and a small test repo.

josh: +1, thanks for the fast repro and PR.
